title: Trace: a setup's own machine and post are honoured all the way to the posted files

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12, after #1206 turned out to be a misreport (the per-setup pick works once "this setup has its own machine" is ticked): "we should trace that it works as intended all the way to output".

The model is `crates/app/src/setup_mount.rs` (#343, #388): a setup owns its mount or follows the document's; every law that judges an existing operation reads that operation's own setup; a program with several mounts posts one file per mount. PR #1222 (draft, test-only, branch `issue/1206-setup-machine-post-per-setup`) already pins the UI picks and that two mounts post two files. What is not pinned end to end is that each stage between the tick and the bytes in the file uses the right machine and the right post.

## The trace (each row is a test; say in the PR which existing test already covers a row instead of duplicating it)
Fixture: Setup1 follows the document (machine A, post A); Setup2 has its own machine B and its own post B, chosen so the difference is visible in the output (different kinematics or limits, different post dialect). Drive the picks through the UI path (as #1222 does) and once through the MCP tools.
1. **Stored:** the document, Setup1 and Setup2 each hold what the page shows.
2. **Generated:** each setup's operations are generated against their own machine while the OTHER setup is active (a limit, spindle or kind law that differs between A and B gives the right verdict per setup).
3. **Verified / simulated:** the machine-dependent checks (travel limits, rotary stack, workholding rpm) read each setup's own machine.
4. **Posted:** one file per mount; each file is written by its own post (assert dialect markers that differ between post A and post B, not just the file count), holds only its own setup's operations, in order, with its own setup's work offset; file names tell the mounts apart.
5. **Follow the document:** change the document's machine and post - Setup1's output changes, Setup2's does not. Then untick Setup2's own machine/post - it follows again, in one undoable step each.
6. **Round trip:** save, reopen, post again - byte-identical files. Undo/redo of the tick and of each pick restores the earlier output.
7. **Edges:** both setups own the same machine and post (how many files, and is that what the model says); own machine with a followed post and the reverse; a setup whose own post does not serve its own machine (refused by name, nothing posted).

## Rules for this work
Tests and a trace table in the PR body; no change to posting or the model. If a row FAILS - a setup posted through a post it does not show, generated or checked against another setup's machine, operations in the wrong file - do not fix it here: file it as its own `P1` `source:agent` issue with the failing test and the readings, leave that test in this PR marked `#[ignore = "<issue>"]`, and say so first in the report.

Done means: the seven rows are each covered by a named test (new or existing), the PR body carries the table row -> test -> result, and every failing row has its own issue.
